cards.name: Color Key
cards.summary: Old one-colour keyer: makes every pixel close to the Key Color transparent, with a hard tolerance and simple edge thin/feather. Produces crunchy, aliased edges compared with modern keyers.
use_for: quick removal of a flat, evenly lit solid-colour background on a graphic or logo
knocking out a pure green/blue plate on low-stakes social reel overlays
legacy projects that already use it
avoid: real green-screen interviews or presenters (use Keylight 1.2 instead)
hair, motion blur or semi-transparent edges (no soft matte, edges chatter)
live-action press photos: the key colour also appears in flags and clothes and punches holes

params.name: Key Color
params.typical: #00B140 for green screen, #0047BB for blue screen (sample the actual plate)

params.name: Color Tolerance
params.does: How far from the key colour a pixel can be and still be removed (0-255)

params.name: Edge Thin
params.does: Shrinks (+) or grows (-) the matte edge in pixels

cards.scripting: Obsolete: prefer Keylight (1.2) (match name 'Keylight 906') or Linear Color Key. Premiere 2026 still has the same legacy Color Key (Keying); Ultra Key is the better Premiere keyer. Key Color is set as "#RRGGBB"; the harvested default is pure blue and Color Tolerance defaults to 0, so applying it with no props removes nothing. Tolerance is in 0-255 units, not percent. The gallery demo (Key Color #A88A53, Color Tolerance 45) does not remove the beige wall cleanly: verified 2026-10-04 it punches scattered hard-edged black/transparent holes in skin shadows, the flowers, a tan clothing patch and patches of the wall, which is exactly the live-footage 'avoid' case.

verified.note: Scattered hard, aliased black (transparent) holes appear wherever pixels match the tan key colour (eyes and skin shadows, flowers, wall patches, a clothing patch), so the one-colour keying is clearly visible.

cards.name: Gaussian Blur (Legacy)
cards.summary: The older Gaussian Blur implementation, kept in Obsolete for old projects: softens the whole layer evenly in both directions or only horizontally/vertically. Same look as the current Gaussian Blur, but it has no Repeat Edge Pixels option and is slower at large radii.
use_for: opening old project templates that already contain it
blur-in / blur-out transitions on titles in legacy comps
soft background plate behind a lower third
avoid: new work: use Gaussian Blur (ADBE Gaussian Blur 2), which is GPU accelerated and handles edges better
large blurs on full-frame footage: edges go dark/transparent because there is no Repeat Edge Pixels

params.name: Blurriness
params.typical: 5-20 for a soft background, 40-100 for a blur transition

cards.scripting: Obsolete: apply 'ADBE Gaussian Blur 2' (Gaussian Blur) instead; its Blurriness and Blur Dimensions behave the same and it adds Repeat Edge Pixels. Premiere equivalent: Gaussian Blur. Keyframe Blurriness for blur-in/out.

verified.note: The whole frame is evenly defocused at Blurriness 25: faces, stripes, foreground blocks and flowers all lose detail in both directions.

cards.name: Lightning
cards.summary: Old Lightning generator: draws an electric bolt between a Start point and an End point over the layer, with zig-zag, side branches, an outside glow colour and an inside core colour; the bolt shape changes over time (Speed, Stability). Superseded in AE by Advanced Lightning.
use_for: a quick electric arc between two words or icons in an explainer
zap accent on a 'shock' moment in a satire reel
energy link between two map points in a trailer graphic
avoid: realistic storm shots (looks like a cheap 2D overlay; use stock lightning footage)
switching Blending Mode to Normal over footage (hard-edged opaque line)
new AE work where Advanced Lightning is available (better glow, obstacles, alpha interaction)

params.name: Start point
params.does: Where the bolt starts, comp pixels

params.name: End point
params.does: Where the bolt ends, comp pixels

params.name: Amplitude
params.does: How far the bolt zig-zags from the straight line

params.name: Speed
params.does: How fast the bolt shape changes

cards.scripting: Obsolete in AE: use Advanced Lightning ('ADBE Lightning 2') for new work. Premiere 2026 has the same legacy Lightning effect (match 'AE.ADBE Lightning'). It composites over the layer it is applied to (default Blending Mode 2 = Add, not 1 Normal), or put it on a black solid set to Add/Screen layer mode. Start/End point are comp pixels [x, y]. Verified 2026-10-04: over the bright test clip the default blend renders the bolt as a near-white zig-zag line and the blue Outside Color glow barely shows; use a darker plate or add Glow for a coloured arc. Blending Mode: 1 Normal, 2 Add, 3 Screen (read from After Effects 26.0). 'Simulation' (0/1) is believed to be the 'Rerun at each frame' checkbox; 'Fixed Endpoint' is 0/1.

verified.note: A white zig-zag bolt with a small side branch runs from (480,540) to (1440,540) across the centre of the untouched clip; the blue outside glow barely reads against the bright background.

cards.name: Luma Key
cards.summary: Old luminance keyer: removes all pixels brighter or darker than a threshold (or near/far from it), with edge thin and feather. Used to drop black or white backgrounds.
use_for: drop the black background of a fire, spark or light-leak stock clip
remove a white page background from a scanned document or newspaper clipping
knock out a black backdrop behind a logo sting
avoid: live-action shots with mid-tones near the threshold (holes in faces and suits)
soft glows: hard threshold clips the falloff (use Screen/Add blend mode or Extract instead)

params.name: Key Type
params.does: Which side of the threshold is removed
params.typical: 2 (Key Out Darker) for black backgrounds, 1 (Key Out Brighter) for white

params.name: Tolerance
params.does: Range around the threshold for Similar/Dissimilar types

cards.scripting: Obsolete: prefer Extract ('ADBE Extract') or simply a Screen/Add layer blend mode for black-background elements. Premiere 2026 has its own Luma Key (match 'AE.ADBE Legacy Key Luma'). Threshold/Tolerance are 0-255 units; with the defaults (Threshold 0) it removes nothing. Key Type: 1 Key Out Brighter, 2 Key Out Darker (default), 3 Key Out Similar, 4 Key Out Dissimilar (read from After Effects 26.0); the 2026-10-04 gallery render shows 1 removing the bright wall.

verified.note: Everything brighter than Threshold 130 (wall, white stripes, highlights) is keyed to black, leaving a ragged high-contrast cut-out of the darker clothing, foreground blocks and red stripes, which confirms Key Type 1 = Key Out Brighter.

cards.name: Path Text
cards.summary: Legacy text generator that draws characters along a Bezier path, circle or line, with per-character jitter and fill/stroke options. Replaced by native text layers with Path Options.
use_for: opening old templates that already contain it
text running around a circle badge in a legacy explainer comp
avoid: new work: use a text layer with a mask and Path Options > Path
anything needing Hindi/Devanagari: the old renderer does not shape complex scripts
cards.scripting: The harvest failed on this effect ("TypeError: null is not an object"), so no property names are known and none can be set from a spec. The text itself is entered in a modal Edit Text dialog that scripts cannot drive (applying it may raise that dialog). Status unusable for the pipeline; it is also obsolete. Use a text layer instead: add a mask, then set textLayer.property('ADBE Text Properties').property('ADBE Text Path Options').property('ADBE Text Path').setValue(maskIndex). No Premiere equivalent (Essential Graphics text cannot follow a path).

verified.note: Card status is unusable (the harvest failed and the text is entered only in a modal dialog), so no gallery frame was rendered.
verified.second_opinion: agree: ground truth has the harvest error 'TypeError: null is not an object' and no props, so nothing can be set; unusable keeps it out of the gallery (no index entry, no frame).

cards.name: Reduce Interlace Flicker
cards.summary: Applies a slight vertical blur to stop thin horizontal lines and fine detail from flickering on interlaced broadcast displays. On progressive 1080p work it just softens the image vertically.
use_for: tame twitter on thin horizontal lines in a ticker or lower-third for an interlaced TV deliverable
soften fine text or pinstripe graphics that shimmer when scaled down
avoid: progressive web/social deliverables (it only blurs)
large Softness values: text turns visibly mushy
cards.scripting: Obsolete in AE: replace with Gaussian Blur set to Blur Dimensions = Vertical and Blurriness 1-2. Premiere 2026 still lists the same Reduce Interlace Flicker effect (match 'AE.ADBE Reduce Interlace Flicker'); the clip's Field Options > Flicker Removal does a similar job. Softness range 0-1000. Measured 2026-10-04 at 1920x1080: Softness 10 matches a vertical-only Gaussian blur of about 4 px sigma, which on the already-soft test clip is invisible at preview size; if it scales linearly, 50 is about 20 px and smears faces into streaks. The gallery demo uses 25 (about 10 px) so the vertical softening shows without wrecking the picture.

verified.note: At Softness 25 the frame is now plainly softened vertically only: block tops, stripes and the centre detail smear up and down while the thin poles and block posts keep their side edges and the faces stay readable, where the old Softness 10 render looked identical to the untouched clip (vertical edge contrast now 33% below the reference against 7% before).

cards.name: Spill Suppressor
cards.summary: Removes green or blue colour spill (reflected screen colour) from the edges and skin of a keyed subject by desaturating the chosen colour. Suppression above 100 over-corrects: the chosen colour is pushed past neutral toward its complement (red turns green).
use_for: clean green fringe on a keyed presenter or interviewee
remove blue cast on hair after a blue-screen key in a legacy comp
avoid: new work: Advanced Spill Suppressor or Keylight's own despill are better
footage with real green/blue objects (shirts, flags, logos lose their colour)
Suppression above ~100: the suppressed colour flips to its complement (red areas and skin turned green at 200)
cards.scripting: Obsolete: apply Advanced Spill Suppressor instead (or Keylight's built-in despill). Place after the keyer in the stack. Premiere has no standalone spill effect; use Ultra Key's Spill Suppression section. Color To Suppress is "#RRGGBB"; harvested default is pure blue. The gallery demo suppresses red (red stripes, foreground blocks) only because the test clip has no green screen. Verified 2026-10-04: at Suppression 200 the red stripes, foreground blocks, flowers and faces flipped to green/teal instead of grey, so the demo now uses 100; the re-render confirmed red goes to neutral grey (faces keep a slight grey-green cast).

verified.note: At Suppression 100 the red stripes, saffron, foreground blocks and flowers now go to a neutral grey (red-area chroma 81 down to 17) while real greens stay green, where the old 200 render overshot them to green/teal; faces keep a slight grey-green cast.

cards.name: mocha shape
cards.summary: Obsolete Imagineer Systems (mocha for AE) importer: renders a tracked spline shape pasted from mocha as a matte, cut-out or filled colour shape on the layer. Nothing happens until mocha shape data is pasted into it, which a script cannot do.
use_for: legacy projects that already contain mocha shape data (blurring a tracked face or number plate)
re-rendering an old tracked screen-replacement matte
avoid: new work: use Boris FX Mocha AE or AE's built-in mask tracking
applying it without pasted mocha data (renders nothing useful)

params.name: Blend mode
params.does: How the shape combines with the layer's alpha

params.name: Render type
params.typical: 1 Shape cutout (default); 2 Color composite, 3 Color shape cutout

params.name: Render edge width
params.does: Whether mocha's feathered edge width is rendered (0/1)

params.name: Shape colour
params.does: Fill colour when rendering a coloured shape

cards.scripting: Needs custom 'Shape data' pasted from mocha (custom type, cannot be set from a spec), and 'Layer name' is also custom, so status needs_input; it is also obsolete. Translation/Scale/Shear/Perspective are written by mocha's export, do not hand-edit. Blend mode: 1 Add, 2 Subtract, 3 Multiply; Render type: 1 Shape cutout, 2 Color composite, 3 Color shape cutout (read from After Effects 26.0). Use Mocha AE (Boris FX, in AE) for new tracking. No Premiere equivalent (use Premiere mask tracking). Confidence low.

verified.note: Card status is needs_input (needs mocha Shape data pasted into a custom property scripts cannot set), so no gallery frame was rendered.
verified.second_opinion: agree: ground truth has 'Shape data' and 'Layer name' as custom properties, so without pasted mocha data it renders nothing useful; needs_input, no gallery entry, param ranges on the card match the harvest.

cards.name: 3D Camera Tracker
cards.summary: Analyses moving footage, solves the real camera's 3D motion and lets you create an AE camera plus null/solid/text anchors that stick to surfaces in the shot. It does not change the picture itself; only coloured track points show. Until the background solve finishes, renders carry AE's blue 'Analyzing in background' banner.
use_for: pin a 3D title or statistic onto a road, wall or stage in drone/handheld B-roll
place a party flag or location label that sticks to a building in a documentary establishing shot
add tracked callouts to a walking-crowd shot in a news reel
screen replacement on a billboard with parallax
avoid: still images or tripod-locked shots: no parallax, the solve fails (use Tripod Pan only for pure pans)
shots dominated by moving people or crowds (bad solve; mask them out)
forgetting to make the attached layers 3D and to create the camera

params.name: Shot Type
params.typical: 1 (Fixed Angle of View) for most footage; zoom shots need the variable-zoom option

params.name: Horizontal Angle of View
params.does: Known lens FOV in degrees, used only when the shot type is 'Specify Angle of View'

params.name: Solve Method
params.does: Scene assumption for the solve (Auto / Typical / Mostly Flat / Tripod Pan...)

params.name: Render Track Points
params.does: Burns the track points into the render (0/1)

params.name: Track Point Size
params.does: Display size of the track points, percent

params.name: Target Size
params.does: Size of the placement target, percent

params.name: Detailed Analysis
params.typical: 0; 1 if the solve error is high

params.name: Auto-delete Points Across Time
params.does: When you delete track points in one frame, the matching points on the same feature are deleted at other times too (0/1)

cards.scripting: Analysis starts automatically in the background after the effect is applied and needs real camera motion with parallax; on a still photo it fails. Verified 2026-10-04: an aerender of a freshly applied instance shows the blue 'Analyzing in background (step 1 of 2)' banner burned across the middle of an otherwise untouched frame and no track points, so let the analysis finish inside AE and save the project before rendering (the harvested 'Hide Warning Banner' 0/1 property may hide it; unverified). Status needs_input: needs moving footage with parallax and a completed, saved solve. Creating the camera/anchors is a UI action on selected track points; scripts cannot pick points, so script-side use is limited to applying it and waiting, or reading the camera it created. Apply it to a plain footage layer; if the layer is time-remapped, a different size from the comp, or has other effects before it, precompose first (same rule as Warp Stabilizer). Shot Type: 1 Fixed Angle of View, 2 Variable Zoom, 3 a separator, 4 Specify Angle of View; Show Track Points: 1 2D Source, 2 3D Solved; Solve Method: 1 Auto Detect, 2 a separator, 3 Typical, 4 Mostly Flat Scene, 5 Tripod Pan (read from After Effects 26.0). No Premiere equivalent.

verified.note: Frame is the untouched clip with AE's blue 'Analyzing in background (step 1 of 2)' banner across the middle and no track points: aerender rendered before the background analysis ran, which no demo value can fix, so status is now needs_input (needs moving footage and a completed solve).
verified.second_opinion: agree: 153.png is the untouched clip with the blue 'Analyzing in background (step 1 of 2)' banner and no track points, same failure as Warp Stabilizer 089.png; needs_input matches that precedent and rerender false is right since the gallery skips needs_input.

previous.why: aerender rendered before the background analysis ran: a harness limit, not an effect fault

cards.name: 3D Glasses
cards.summary: Combines a left-eye and a right-eye layer into a stereoscopic image: red/cyan style anaglyph, side-by-side, over-under, interlaced or difference views, with convergence and vertical alignment.
use_for: retro red/blue anaglyph look for a '3D cinema' themed reel title
stereo deliverable from two rendered eye views
checking stereo alignment with the Difference view
avoid: using it as a simple RGB-split / chromatic-aberration glitch: VR Chromatic Aberrations or three Shift Channels copies offset in Position are easier
large convergence offsets on text (eye strain, unreadable)

params.name: Scene Convergence
params.does: Horizontal offset between the two views (sets where the image sits in depth)

params.name: 3D View
params.does: Output format: stereo pair, over-under, interlace, coloured anaglyphs, difference
params.typical: 6 Red Green LR or 7 Red Blue LR for the retro anaglyph

params.name: Balance
params.does: Colour balance for the balanced anaglyph modes

cards.scripting: Left View and Right View are layer-reference properties: the spec system cannot set them; in ExtendScript use eff.property('Left View').setValue(leftLayer.index) (0 = None). With both set to None it may use the layer itself, which only gives an offset tint, not true stereo (unverified). 3D View (read from After Effects 26.0): 1 Stereo Pair (Side by Side), 2 Over Under, 3 Interlace Upper L Lower R, 4 Difference, 6 Red Green LR, 7 Red Blue LR, 9 Balanced Red Green LR, 10 Balanced Red Blue LR, 12 Balanced Colored Red Blue (5, 8, 11 are separators). No Premiere equivalent.

verified.note: Card status is needs_input (Left View/Right View are layer references a spec cannot set), so no gallery frame was rendered; gallery 231 is the different obsolete 'ADBE 3D Glasses' effect.
verified.second_opinion: agree: Left View/Right View are layer-reference properties (ground truth type 'layer'), the same reason Blend, Set Matte and Difference Matte are needs_input; gallery index 231 is 'ADBE 3D Glasses' (the obsolete card in ae_effect_25), not this 'ADBE 3D Glasses2'.

cards.name: Bevel Alpha
cards.summary: Adds a chiselled, lit bevel along the alpha edges of a layer, giving text, logos and cut-outs a raised embossed look. On a full-frame clip it only bevels the outer frame edge.
use_for: raised look on a party logo or channel bug
embossed title text for a documentary chapter card
give a cut-out photo of a leader a picture-frame edge in an explainer
button-like lower-third plates
avoid: thick edges with high intensity (dated 2000s WordArt look)
thin or Devanagari text at small sizes (bevel fills the strokes)

params.name: Edge Thickness
params.does: Width of the bevel in pixels

params.name: Light Angle
params.does: Direction the light comes from, degrees

cards.scripting: Works on the alpha channel, so on an opaque full-frame clip the bevel only appears at the 1920x1080 frame border (the demo shows a framed border, not a change in the picture). Best on text, shape layers, logos with alpha or masked cut-outs. Light Angle has no harvested range: raw degrees. Not in the Premiere 2026 effect list (no equivalent); in Premiere build the bevel in AE and bring it in via Dynamic Link.

verified.note: On the opaque full-frame clip only the frame border is bevelled: a white lit edge along the top/left and a dark shaded edge on the right/bottom, with the picture unchanged inside, as the scripting note says.

cards.name: Bevel Edges
cards.summary: Gives the layer's rectangular bounds a hard, lit 3D bevel, like a tile or a raised picture frame. Unlike Bevel Alpha it uses the layer edges, not the alpha shape.
use_for: framed photo / archival picture inset in a documentary
tile look for a split-screen grid of leaders in a political explainer
button-style plates behind numbers or stats
avoid: thickness above ~0.2 (looks like a 90s screensaver)
using it on text or irregular cut-outs (bevels the box, not the shape: use Bevel Alpha)

params.name: Edge Thickness
params.does: Bevel width as a fraction of the layer size (0-0.5)

params.name: Light Intensity
params.does: Strength of light/shade on the bevel (0-1)

cards.scripting: Edge Thickness is a fraction of the layer size, not pixels (0.1 on a 1920 layer is a thick ~100 px bevel). Scale the layer down (e.g. 70%) so the bevelled tile reads against a background. Light Angle has no harvested range: raw degrees. Not in the Premiere 2026 effect list (no equivalent).

verified.note: A thick tile bevel frames the layer bounds: bright white top/left faces and dark right/bottom faces with mitred corners, the picture inset like a raised panel.
